title: Governor of Idaho

context.text: Incumbent Republican Gov. Brad Little is seeking a third term.
Republican primary (May 19, 2026): Little won renomination with 58.96% of the vote, ahead of Mark Fitzpatrick (28.79%) and six other candidates.
Democratic primary (May 19, 2026): attorney Terri Pickens won with 61.42%, ahead of Jill Kirkham (16.96%), Maxine Durand (14.54%) and Chanelle Torrez (7.09%).

John Stegner, a former Idaho Supreme Court justice, is running as an independent. Libertarian Paul Sand and Constitution Party nominee Pro-Life (a legal name change from Marvin Richardson) hold their parties' ballot lines. Jacob Burnett is a declared independent write-in candidate and will not be printed on the ballot.
Idaho's Proposition 1, a ballot initiative on abortion rights, is also on the November ballot, and the candidates were asked about it in the Idaho Capital Sun voter guide.

candidates.name: Brad Little
candidates.ballotNote: Won the May 19 Republican primary with 58.96%. Idaho does not elect a running mate; the lieutenant governor is elected separately.

summary.text: Brad Little is the incumbent Republican governor of Idaho, seeking a third term. A rancher by background, he served as a state senator (2001–2009) and lieutenant governor (2009–2019) before being elected governor in 2018 and re-elected in 2022. As governor he signed the 2025 Idaho parental choice tax credit, a Medicaid cost-containment law that he said does not reject the voters' Medicaid expansion, and a 2022 income-tax cut.

background.text: Graduated from the University of Idaho with a B.S. in 1976 and ran his family's ranching operation.
Appointed state senator in 2001, lieutenant governor in 2009 (appointed by Gov. Butch Otter) and elected governor in 2018; re-elected in 2022 over Democrat Stephen Heidt and independent Ammon Bundy.

priorities.text: Campaign materials describe his goal as making Idaho a place where people have the opportunity to thrive.
Little did not respond to the Idaho Capital Sun voter-guide questionnaire, so no issue answers in his own words are available there.

record.text: Signed House Bill 93, establishing the Idaho parental choice tax credit and an advance-payment fund; the House passed it 42–28 and the Senate 20–15.
Signed House Bill 345, the Medicaid Reform and Cost Containment Act, saying it improves the program 'without rejecting the will of the voters on Medicaid Expansion.'
Signed House Bill 436, his 'Leading Idaho' income tax relief bill providing a $350 million one-time rebate and $251 million in ongoing tax relief by lowering income tax brackets.

candidates.name: Terri Pickens
candidates.ballotNote: Won the May 19 Democratic primary with 61.42%.
candidates.currentRole: Attorney; 2022 Democratic nominee for lieutenant governor

summary.text: Terri Pickens is the Democratic nominee for governor. An attorney and fourth-generation Idahoan from Pocatello, she was the party's 2022 nominee for lieutenant governor. Her stated priorities are preventing a nuclear waste storage campus in Idaho, housing affordability and removing the food tax, and restoring funding for public schools and rural hospitals; she supports Proposition 1 and wants to repeal the private-school tax credit.

background.text: Attorney who started and runs her own small business, and has served on nonprofit boards; fourth-generation Idahoan from Pocatello.
Democratic nominee for lieutenant governor in 2022.

priorities.text: Top priorities: keeping Idaho from becoming a nuclear waste site, addressing housing affordability and removing the food tax, and ending 'culture wars' to refocus on public schools, rural hospitals, the homeowners' exemption and wildfire preparedness.
Revisit recent tax cuts and re-fund services such as schools, rural hospitals, roads and bridges, and community policing.

positions.summary: Supports Proposition 1, the ballot initiative to end Idaho's abortion ban.
Wants to repeal the state's private education tax credit.
positions.quote: Repeal. This program is set to explode in cost, as it has in other states.

positions.summary: Said at an Oct. 6 forum that her first budget would restore Medicaid expansion.
positions.quote: It's going to restore Medicaid expansion.

statements.quote: For me, there won't be any 287(g) agreements for us to be having these discussions as to how we can support and train these folks.
statements.context: At the Oct. 6, 2026 League of Women Voters of Idaho forum, per Idaho Capital Sun

statements.quote: The State can find ways to speed the housing construction process by adjusting rules for builders and developers.
statements.context: In the Idaho Capital Sun voter guide

statements.quote: I will revisit those cuts for billionaires and re-fund the services, such as schools, rural hospitals, roads and bridges, and community policing
statements.context: In the Idaho Capital Sun voter guide, on the 2026 budget cuts and tax cuts

candidates.researchNotes: Quotes from the Idaho Capital Sun voter guide and its Oct. 6 forum report. terriforidaho.com loaded, but its issues pages were not reviewed.

candidates.name: John Stegner
candidates.currentRole: Mediator; former Idaho Supreme Court justice (2018–2023)

summary.text: John Stegner is an independent candidate for governor. He was a state district judge from 1997 to 2018 and an Idaho Supreme Court justice from 2018 to 2023, and is known for starting drug and treatment courts. His priorities are keeping public lands public, fully funding public education (including repealing the private-school tax credit), and expanding access to medical care.

background.text: Earned a B.A. from Whitman College in 1977 and a J.D. from the University of Idaho College of Law in 1982.
Served as a state district judge in Idaho's second judicial district (1997–2018), then as an Idaho Supreme Court justice (2018–2023).

priorities.text: Top three priorities: keeping public lands in public hands, ensuring Idaho fulfills its constitutional obligation to fund public education, and increasing access to medical care.
Reinstating Medicaid access for the roughly 42,000 Idahoans he says lost coverage this year.

positions.summary: Supports repealing the private-school tax credit, saying it diverts about $50 million from public education.
Says he would support legislation to reinstate Medicaid access to those who recently lost it.
positions.quote: I would support legislation that would reinstate access to the 42,000 recently removed from Medicaid access.

statements.quote: I would not have entered into the agreement with ICE had I been the governor
statements.context: At the Oct. 6, 2026 League of Women Voters of Idaho forum, per Idaho Capital Sun, on the state's 287(g) agreement

candidates.researchNotes: Added statements from the Idaho Capital Sun voter guide and its Oct. 6 forum report.

candidates.name: Paul Sand

summary.text: Paul Sand is the Libertarian Party nominee for governor; he says he won the party's 2022 gubernatorial primary and served 10 years on the White Bird City Council. His listed occupation is software engineer, computer-business entrepreneur and home builder.

priorities.text: Ending the divide between rural and urban counties.
priorities.quote: My only priority is to permanently eliminate the division between conservative rural counties and liberal urban counties

priorities.text: Letting counties opt out of state government and set their own taxes and programs.
priorities.quote: I would allow counties to opt out of being involved in the state government entirely and self-rule themselves and set their own taxes on their own programs

candidates.researchNotes: He did not answer the Idaho Capital Sun general-election questionnaire; quotes come from his answers in its primary guide and a May 11, 2026 BYU-Idaho Radio interview. No campaign site was reached. No positions on the guide's issues were stated directly.

statements.quote: We do not want low-income housing developments, we do not want data centers and more outsiders moving in, period.
statements.context: In the Idaho Capital Sun 2026 primary voter guide (May 2026)

candidates.name: Pro-Life

summary.text: Pro-Life, who legally changed his name from Marvin Richardson, is the Constitution Party nominee for governor.

candidates.researchNotes: Did not respond to the Idaho Capital Sun questionnaire; no campaign website, forum appearance or other coverage found.

candidates.name: Jacob Burnett

summary.text: Jacob Burnett, 30, of Middleton, is running as an independent write-in candidate. His stated priorities are agency audits and lobbying transparency, lowering personal property taxes and slowing speculative out-of-state development, and expanded telehealth and parental choice in education.

priorities.text: Audits of state agencies and transparent lobbying rules.
priorities.quote: restoring accountability through sweeping audits of state agencies, transparent lobbying rules, and an end to backroom deals

priorities.text: Lowering or eliminating personal property taxes and slowing speculative out-of-state development.
priorities.quote: protecting property and affordability by lowering or eliminating personal property taxes for residents, slowing speculative out-of-state development

priorities.text: Expanded telehealth, more local providers, and parental choice and disclosure in education.
priorities.quote: strengthening healthcare and education access with expanded telehealth services, expanding treatment options, training more local providers, and giving parents real choice and disclosure in their children's education

positions.summary: Supports abortion access through the first trimester with exceptions, says he does not oppose Proposition 1's broader rights provisions in principle but does not support removing all limits or oversight, and says he would respect the result if voters pass it.
Supports keeping Idaho's private education tax credit.

candidates.researchNotes: All from his answers in the Idaho Capital Sun voter guide; no campaign website found.
candidates.ballotNote: Declared independent write-in candidate; not printed on the ballot.

statements.quote: I don't think the answer is simply building faster, much of our shortage has been driven by speculative, out-of-state investment and large-scale development that prioritizes corporate profit over resident ownership.
statements.context: In the Idaho Capital Sun voter guide

statements.quote: I'd also enforce rent regulations tied to actual property upkeep/direct value

researchNotes: Idaho elects its lieutenant governor separately; there are no running mates. Little did not respond to the Idaho Capital Sun questionnaire, so his positions rest on bills he signed. Ballotpedia was blocked from this environment (bot challenge). Primary results come from the Idaho Secretary of State's official canvass report. The Secretary of State's general-election candidate list could not be loaded (the VoteIdaho.gov candidate-list page still shows the 2024 list and no 2026 file was found; county sites were checked without finding a sample ballot); the slate (Little, Pickens, Stegner, Sand, Pro-Life) rests on the Idaho Capital Sun voter guide, the Wikipedia race page and The Green Papers (which tracks Secretary of State filings), and Green Papers lists Burnett as an independent write-in. Little's pre-2019 legislative votes were not researched. Pickens has no campaign website found in this research pass. The slate is also consistent with the Idaho Capital Sun's May 28, 2026 post-primary roundup (Little, Pickens, Stegner, Sand, Pro-Life).
